title: Orbital: CelesTrak TLEs and SGP4 on the globe, gravity encoder and precession in the bridge
shape: TLE -> SGP4 -> position is a forecast whose error grows with epoch age. GEV draws it; the bridge has the potential-energy encoder and a drift detector but no orbit.
flow: epoch age ──▶ trend.py scope  'error < X km' with X ~ 1 km/day   (bridge)
geoid.js: h = H + N    every altitude in GEV passes through here; record the datum

notes.bottleneck: No second position source in GEV, so a TLE-age residual has no anchor. The INSTRUMENT route needs one (FCL open problem 5a).
notes.leverage: getNextIssPass already computes link windows; orbital-phycom consumes exactly that and nothing else in the ecosystem does.
notes.harmonics: precession.py and celestialRing.js both place the pole; a cross-check costs one function call and can fail.
notes.tertiary: Altitude datums: ellipsoidal in GEV, orthometric in most sources, pressure altitude in ADS-B. A reading that omits its datum is off by up to ~100 m and looks fine.

gev.role: twoline2satrec/propagate from satellite.js; ISS overlay; dense catalog modes; tracked refresh
findNextIssPass(): look angles, next pass above min elevation
Launch Library 2 rolling 30-day; failed launches get no fallback orbit

celestial directions projected into the camera plane

drift toward a band edge over a measurement log (with TRD-1..7 recorded)
adaptive octree; ENG-5: one point per leaf, batch before trusting it

directional navigation; celestialRing is a compass rendered on a globe
AI-verifiable technology library; SGP4 and EGM96 are verifiable references to register

avenues.title: SGP4 state -> gravity encoder payload
avenues.moves: per-satellite r, v from propagate() -> specific potential -> GravityBridgeEncoder.from_geometry(); one 39-bit token per satellite per epoch
avenues.fails_if: the encoder's band edges are set for planetary-scale potentials and every LEO satellite lands in one band; then the payload carries no information and the null harness (repo_guard.null_harness) says so

avenues.title: TLE epoch age as a drift claim
avenues.moves: epoch age per NORAD id -> trend.py scope; claim 'position error < X km' with X growing ~1 km/day; GEV's stale flag becomes a band edge instead of a boolean
avenues.fails_if: there is no second position source, so the residual is unmeasurable in GEV alone; INSTRUMENT needs an anchor (FCL open problem 5a). A ground-station pass time is the cheapest anchor and orbital-phycom is where it lives

avenues.title: precession.py vs celestialRing.js cross-check
avenues.moves: both place celestial directions; compute the pole position at J2000 from each and compare
avenues.fails_if: they disagree by more than precession.py's stated model error (a few arcmin over reference epochs); one of them then has a datum bug and the comparison says which

avenues.title: ISS pass windows as orbital-phycom link opportunities
avenues.moves: getNextIssPass({lat, lon, minElevDeg}) -> a link-window record the orbital-phycom simulations can consume
avenues.fails_if: orbital-phycom's core/ expects a different orbit representation than look angles; then the seam is a schema and not a function

interference: GEV altitudes are ellipsoidal (h); barometric/ADS-B altitudes are orthometric or pressure altitudes. geoid.js is the one place that reconciles them. Any bridge reading of a GEV altitude must record which datum it took
satellite.js SGP4 is a mean-element propagator; feeding its output to a Keplerian helper (orbital_velocity from potential) mixes models. Fine for a Gray band, wrong for a residual below ~1 km
